_sources.discrepancies: [2026-06-10] Corrected the 2026 primary date from 2026-05-05 to Tuesday, March 3, 2026 (NCSBE): registration deadline Feb 6, one-stop early voting Feb 12-28. Removed the previously listed 2026-07-07 'primary runoff' entry: North Carolina's reserved second-primary date was May 12, 2026, held only if a runoff-eligible candidate requested one; as of 2026-06-10 NCSBE's Upcoming Election page lists the Nov 3, 2026 general as the next statewide election, so no second-primary entry is carried. General: registration deadline Oct 9, early voting Oct 15-31 (NCSBE). In-person registration deadlines are set to the last day of one-stop early voting because NC same-day registration is not available on Election Day.

earlyVoting.notes: One-stop early voting with same-day registration ran February 12-28, 2026 for the March 3 primary. Hours and locations set by county boards of elections (NCSBE).

One-stop early voting with same-day registration runs October 15-31, 2026 (ends 3 p.m. Oct 31). Regular registration deadline is October 9; same-day registration is available only during early voting, not on Election Day. Hours and locations set by county boards: https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-early-person

One-stop early voting includes same-day registration and runs October 15-31, 2026 for the general election. Exact locations and hours set by each county board of elections: https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/vote-early-person

acceptedIds: North Carolina driver's license or DMV-issued ID
Veterans ID card issued by the U.S. Dept. of Veterans Affairs
Tribal enrollment card issued by a federally recognized tribe
Student ID from a North Carolina university or college (public or private)
votingRules.expirationRule: Photo ID must not be expired. Voters aged 65+ may use an expired ID if it was unexpired on their 65th birthday. Details: https://www.ncsbe.gov/voting/voter-id
votingRules.impedimentDeclaration: Voters without an acceptable photo ID may cast a provisional ballot by completing a reasonable impediment form citing a reasonable impediment to obtaining ID.
votingRules.phonesAtPollsDetail: North Carolina allows voters to bring phones into the polling place. Voters may not use phones to take photos of their own or others' ballots. No electioneering within 50 feet of the entrance to a voting place.
additionalRules: Semi-closed primary: registered party members vote in their party's primary. Unaffiliated voters may choose to vote in any party's primary.

North Carolina has runoffs for statewide and federal offices when no candidate receives 30% of the vote in the primary. Runoffs are not party-locked — any eligible registered voter may vote in the runoff regardless of which primary they voted in.

eligibility: Any registered voter may request an absentee ballot without providing a reason
voteByMail.applicationDeadline: Received by the county board of elections by the Tuesday before the election
voteByMail.returnDeadline: Must be received by the county board by 7:30 p.m. on Election Day, or postmarked by Election Day and received within 3 days after
voteByMail.returnDeadlinePlain: Must arrive at the county board by poll closing on Election Day, or be postmarked by Election Day and received within 3 days after.

runoffRules.ruleExplanation: North Carolina rule (N.C. Gen. Stat. §163-110): if no candidate receives 30% of the vote in the primary, a second primary (runoff) is held between the top two candidates. If you voted in one party's primary, you may only vote in that same party's second primary. Unaffiliated voters who did not vote in any first primary may choose which party's second primary to vote in.

primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEn: North Carolina has an open primary (N.C. Gen. Stat. §163-119). Registered voters of a party vote in their party's primary. Unaffiliated voters may choose which party's primary to participate in. If a runoff (second primary) occurs and you voted in a party's first primary, you must vote in that same party's runoff.
primaryParticipation.ruleExplanationEs: Carolina del Norte tiene una primaria abierta (N.C. Gen. Stat. §163-119). Los votantes registrados en un partido votan en la primaria de su partido. Los votantes sin afiliación pueden elegir en qué primaria de partido participar. Si hay una segunda vuelta y votó en la primera primaria de un partido, debe votar en la segunda vuelta de ese mismo partido.
